author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
note: Self-reliance first; courage as the nerve to trust your own convictions.

author: Emily Dickinson
note: No 'hope' theme in the set; read as quiet endurance that never stops. Calm would be the alternative.

author: Seneca
note: Purpose added because the line works as a nudge to stop procrastinating.

author: William Shakespeare
note: In the play it urges a murder; as a reminder it reads purely as resolve.

author: Henry David Thoreau
note: The woods are the setting, not the point, so no nature tag. The point is living deliberately before death.

author: Rabindranath Tagore
note: Acceptance of loss so you can see what is still here; sun and stars imagery adds nature.

author: L. M. Montgomery
note: Time here means daily renewal, not mortality; calm for self-forgiveness.

author: Lao Tzu
note: Starting small on big work. Could also read as patience (time), but time in this set leans toward mortality.

author: Lewis Carroll
note: Tagged for the wonder half of 'nature and wonder' (imagination and openness); there is no nature content.

author: Virginia Woolf
note: A plunge into the morning air with joy. Wonder is primary; courage for the leap. Hard to tag.

author: Robert Louis Stevenson
note: Process over arrival. Calm (letting go of outcomes) is a possible second tag.

author: Alfred, Lord Tennyson
note: Time for 'made weak by time', about holding on to resolve as you age.

author: Willa Cather
note: In the novel this is lying in a garden in the sun. Read as wonder and peaceful surrender.

author: Oscar Wilde
note: Hope and aspiration despite circumstances; the stars stand for wonder. Purpose would also fit.

author: John Keats
note: Beauty and wonder first; time because the beauty never passes into nothingness.

author: Kabir
note: The answer is within, so stop restless searching. Self is primary; calm for ending the wandering.

author: Frances Hodgson Burnett
note: Persisting with something new until it gets done. Wonder is mentioned but is not the point.

author: Okakura Kakuzō
note: Humility about yourself (self) and noticing the worth of others (love). Hard to tag.

author: Sojourner Truth
note: It mentions work, but the point is strength and equal worth, so no purpose tag.

author: William Blake
note: Wonder in small things. Time because of 'Eternity in an hour'.

author: Percy Bysshe Shelley
note: Read as 'hard seasons pass' (acceptance). Courage (endurance) is the alternative.

author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
note: Nature is used for daily beauty and wonder through art; there is no nature content. Self for tending the inner life.

author: John Donne
note: Belonging and connection. The source is a meditation on death, but this line is not about mortality.
